parsed_output.analysis:
The model introduces two states and transitions that are not described anywhere in the specification: OperationalState → ClampingLoseState and the ClampingLoseState itself. It also adds a transition from BrakingState back to InitialState that is not grounded in the spec (the spec only says signal feedback returns the system to the initial state generically, but it's ambiguous whether this applies to BrakingState as well as OperationalState). The core flow (Initial -> Braking -> Clamping, Initial -> Operational on failure, feedback returning to Initial) is present, but the extra state/transition is a clear addition beyond spec scope.</analysis>
<parameter name="issues">
<issue>
<issue>Unspecified state and transition: ClampingLoseState and the transition OperationalState --> ClampingLoseState</issue>
<where>Model: "OperationalState --> ClampingLoseState : Transition to Clamping Lose State" and "ClampingLoseState : Clamping Lose State"</where>
<reason>The specification only describes three states (initial, braking, operational) and one further transition from braking to the brake-caliper-clamping state. There is no mention of an "operational" state leading to any "clamping lose" state, nor any concept of losing clamping. This is an invented state/transition with no basis in the spec, and it introduces behavior not authorized by the natural-language description.</reason>
</issue>
<issue>
<issue>Extra transition: BrakingState --> InitialState (Signal Feedback Sent)</issue>
<where>Model: "BrakingState --> InitialState : Signal Feedback Sent"</where>
<reason>Per the specification, the sequence is: Initial -> Braking (on signal received) -> Clamping (entering clamping state); separately, Initial -> Operational (on failure) -> back to Initial (on feedback sent). The spec's "signal feedback sent" returning to the initial state is naturally tied to the operational path, not to the braking path, since braking is stated to always proceed onward to the clamping state ("After entering the braking state, the system transitions to the brake caliper clamping state"), implying braking has only one exit path (to clamping), not back to initial. Adding a return transition from BrakingState to InitialState contradicts the deterministic single-exit description of the braking state.</reason>
</issue>
</issue>

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1 This state machine model represents the train's basic braking device, which serves as the final execution unit for train braking operations. 
2 When the basic braking device receives a brake signal, it transitions from the initial state to the braking state. If the signal transmission fails, it proceeds to the operational state. Once the signal feedback is sent, it returns to the initial state. 
3 After entering the braking state, the system transitions to the brake caliper clamping state.

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
[*] --> InitialState
InitialState: Initial State

InitialState --> BrakingState : Brake Signal Received
InitialState --> OperationalState : Signal Transmission Fails

BrakingState --> ClampingState : Entering Clamping State
ClampingState : Brake Caliper Clamping State

OperationalState --> InitialState : Signal Feedback Sent
BrakingState --> InitialState : Signal Feedback Sent

OperationalState --> ClampingLoseState : Transition to Clamping Lose State
ClampingLoseState : Clamping Lose State
@enduml
